name: Sicily
train_access: Good regional network; Palermo–Catania 2.5hrs; direct trains to mainland via Villa San Giovanni ferry
hospital: Palermo, Catania, Enna — all with good facilities
summary: Sicily has the most active €1 programmes in Italy. Despite Zone 1 seismic classification, inland elevated towns (500m+) dramatically reduce both earthquake and tsunami risk. Summer temperatures 20–28°C at altitude. Strong Airbnb market in historic villages. 7% flat tax available in most qualifying municipalities.
safety_note: Focus on towns above 500m elevation: Troina (1121m), Gangi (1015m), Petralia Soprana (1147m) are safest. Avoid coastal lowland areas.

name: Sardinia
flood_risk: very low (dry Mediterranean climate; September–October rain possible)
tsunami_risk: none (geologically stable island, no active faults)
incentive_programs: Work from Sardinia digital nomad initiatives
nearest_major_city: Cagliari (intl airport) / Sassari (Alghero airport) / Olbia (intl airport)
train_access: Limited regional rail; best accessed by car; ferries from Civitavecchia (Rome), Genoa, Livorno
hospital: Cagliari (university hospital), Sassari, Nuoro — good quality
summary: The SAFEST region in all of Italy — the only region with no earthquake risk (Zone 4). No tsunami risk. Low flood risk. Island feeling, authentic Sardinian culture, excellent food and wine (Cannonau, Vermentino). 7% flat tax available everywhere. Ferry required for car travel to mainland. Best for buyers who prioritise seismic safety above all else.
safety_note: Italy's only seismically inactive region. No active fault lines. Completely safe from earthquakes and tsunamis.

name: Abruzzo
tsunami_risk: none (inland / Adriatic coast only, no major historical tsunamis)
incentive_programs: Tuscany-style renovation grants in mountain towns
nearest_major_city: Pescara (intl airport, 85km from most towns) / L'Aquila (trains to Rome 2hrs)
hospital: L'Aquila (university hospital), Pescara, Chieti, Lanciano — excellent coverage
summary: One of Italy's most beautiful and unspoiled regions. Three national parks (Gran Sasso, Majella, Abruzzo Lazio Molise). Zone 2 risk — real but manageable; buildings are now earthquake-reinforced post 2009 L'Aquila event. Modern infrastructure. 2hrs from Rome. Excellent skiing, hiking, Adriatic coast. Growing Airbnb market.
safety_note: Zone 2 seismic risk. The 2009 L'Aquila earthquake (M6.3) was the most recent major event. New construction standards are high. Choose towns with modern infrastructure.

name: Molise
nearest_major_city: Campobasso (trains to Naples) / Isernia / Termoli (Adriatic coast)
train_access: Campobasso–Naples 2.5hrs; regional connections across the region
summary: Italy's least-visited and second-smallest region — genuinely hidden. Combines the €1 house programme with a €27,000 relocation grant (paid monthly over 3 years) for qualified applicants who move to towns under 2,000 population. Medieval castles, Samnite ruins, clean rivers, and virtually no tourist crowds. Zone 2 seismic risk.
safety_note: Zone 2 seismic risk, similar to Abruzzo. The combination of €1 house + €27K relocation grant is unmatched anywhere in Italy.

name: Puglia (Apulia)
flood_risk: low (flat limestone plateau; flash floods rare)
tsunami_risk: low (Adriatic coast less exposed; Salento moderate)
incentive_programs: €1 house schemes — Biccari, Candela, Caprarica di Lecce
Biccari online catalogue including pre-renovated homes €7.5K–13K
nearest_major_city: Bari (intl airport, high-speed to Rome/Naples/Milan) / Brindisi (intl airport) / Lecce
train_access: Excellent — Bari is a high-speed rail hub. Lecce–Rome 5hrs direct. Frecciarossa to Milan 4hrs
hospital: Bari (university hospital, excellent), Lecce, Foggia, Brindisi — all good
summary: Italy's top Airbnb destination after Tuscany. Trulli, masserie (farm estates), whitewashed towns and the world's best mozzarella. Biccari's pre-renovated home catalogue (€7.5K–13K) eliminates renovation risk. Bari is Italy's most connected southern hub. Zone 2 seismic, but Puglia has no history of major earthquakes in recent decades.
safety_note: Zone 2 but historically less active than Abruzzo or Sicily. Inland elevated towns (Biccari 640m) significantly safer.

name: Campania
tsunami_risk: none (inland towns; Vesuvius coastal risk N/A for hill villages)
incentive_programs: €1 house schemes — Zungoli, Pietramelara, Bisaccia, Teora, Altavilla Silentina
nearest_major_city: Naples (intl airport, high-speed trains) / Salerno / Avellino / Caserta
train_access: Naples is a major Frecciarossa hub — Rome 1hr, Milan 3hrs. Caserta 30min from Naples
hospital: Naples (multiple major hospitals), Salerno, Avellino, Caserta — excellent coverage
summary: Access to Italy's most vibrant southern city (Naples), incredible food culture, UNESCO sites (Pompeii, Paestum, Caserta Palace), Amalfi Coast. Hill town programmes are well-run with good English support. Zone 2 seismic; 1980 Irpinia earthquake was significant but buildings are now extensively retrofitted.
safety_note: Zone 2 seismic risk. 1980 Irpinia earthquake affected this area. Choose well-rebuilt towns with modern retrofitting. Avoid Vesuvius exclusion zone (30km radius from summit).

name: Piedmont (Alps & Hills)
flood_risk: low (elevated towns; avoid Po River valley floor)
incentive_programs: Some Tuscan-style mountain grants in declining areas
nearest_major_city: Turin (intl airport, TGV to Paris 3.5hrs) / Milan (Malpensa, 1.5hrs) / Genoa (Liguria coast 1hr)
train_access: Excellent — Turin is a TGV hub with direct high-speed to Paris, Lyon, Milan. Asti 1hr from Turin
hospital: Turin (multiple world-class hospitals), Asti, Cuneo, Vercelli — excellent quality
summary: Zone 3 (low risk) — much safer than the south. No €1 programmes but properties under €65K still exist in mountain valleys and Apennine villages. UNESCO Langhe and Monferrato wine hills. Turin–Paris direct TGV. Excellent for wine tourism Airbnb. No tsunami or flood risk in elevated towns.
safety_note: Zone 3 low seismic risk. No earthquake history in recent decades for elevated areas. Avoid Po River flood plain (Turin suburbs); choose hill towns.

name: Lombardy (Alps & Pre-Alps)
incentive_programs: Some Lombardy regional renovation grants for mountain towns
nearest_major_city: Milan (Malpensa intl airport, 1.5hrs) / Bergamo (Ryanair hub, 1hr from most towns)
train_access: Milan is Italy's best-connected hub — TGV to Paris 3.5hrs, Zurich 2.5hrs, Geneva 2hrs, Frankfurt 4hrs
summary: Italy's most expensive region for property but pre-Alpine valleys still offer properties under €70K. Zone 3 (low risk). Unparalleled train connections to all of Europe. Milan Malpensa 1.5hrs from most towns. No earthquake or tsunami risk in mountain valleys. Best for buyers prioritising European connectivity over budget.
safety_note: Zone 3 low seismic risk. Mountain valleys completely safe from tsunamis and floods. Most convenient for international travel (Milan hub).
